summary: The original is a continuously re-igniting red flame field around a drifting dark-indigo portal core on a ~2.05 s cycle; the port's 'portal' expands monotonically from a 6-px seed and swallows the whole rig within ~6.5 s, after which every pixel is frozen at a uniform violet (63,3,184) for at least 240 s with no animation at all.
observations: Controls: both sides expose ZERO settable controls (meta.json sides.orig.controls == [] and sides.port.controls == []); --probe-controls confirms 'no settable controls' on both. Control surface therefore matches; there is nothing to dial.
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors: false on both, sensors: 'off'), so the beat120 feed is irrelevant here.

ORIGINAL, steady state (--skip 40, 20 s @ 20 fps): meanBrightness avg 23.5 (min 14, max 35), meanR avg 61.3, meanG avg 1.8, meanB avg 7.4, motion avg 8.9, motionLit avg 10.6, zeroMotionFrames 0/400, brightnessTrend steady. It never settles down.
PORT, same window (--skip 40, 20 s @ 20 fps): meanBrightness pinned at 82-83, meanB pinned at 181, motion avg 0 (max 1), motionLit avg 0.1, zeroMotionFrames 393/400. Effectively a still image.

Exact port steady-state pixels (--dump at t=40, 40.15, 40.3, 41, 45, 49.9 s): pixels 1..59 are byte-identical (63,3,184) at EVERY dumped time; only pixel 0 flickers (106,3,0 / 57,1,0 / 19,0,0 / 0,0,0 / 51,4,0 / 0,0,0). So the port is not dim-and-slow, it is genuinely frozen — one pixel of residual animation out of 60.

Port's approach to that state (--dump at t=0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 s): at t=0 only pixels 36-41 are lit (a ~6-px seed: 239,115,1 / 21,1,61 / 61,3,177 / 46,2,133 / 3,0,9 / 89,2,0). The lit region then expands OUTWARD in both directions and never contracts — left edge px 36 (t=0) -> 32 (0.5 s) -> 28 (1 s) -> 22 (2 s) -> 12 (4 s) -> 0 (8 s); right edge px 41 -> 45 -> 49 -> 55 -> 59 (clamped by 4 s). Everything the front has passed latches to the constant violet (63,3,184).
The runaway is scale-relative, not a fixed pixel count: on a 16x16 grid rig (256 px) the port fills the entire rig by ~7 s and stays uniform violet for the rest of a 20 s window.

The runaway is NOT frame-rate coupling: the port's fill time (meanBrightness reaching 80) is 6.90 s @ 10 fps, 6.45 s @ 20 fps, 6.38 s @ 40 fps — time-based within noise. The bug is a missing reset/decay, not a per-frame step.

ORIGINAL structure (60-px strip, --dump at 0.1 s spacing over t=40..44.4 s): a contiguous ~19-20 px dark-indigo 'portal core' (peak RGB about 18,0,72; blue channel plateaus at exactly 72, i.e. clipped) occupies roughly pixels 20-40, with the remaining ~35-40 pixels carrying a red-only flame texture (typically 25-34 pixels above R=30, peaks up to R=255 with G<=35 and B=0).

ORIGINAL temporal cycle: autocorrelation of the meanBrightness series over the late 20 s window (20 fps) peaks at lag 41 frames = 2.05 s, with clean harmonics at 82, 123 and 164 frames. Per cycle the core ignites instantly to its blue=72 plateau, holds it for ~1.0 s, then fades exponentially to blue<=2 over the next ~1.0 s, then re-ignites. Measured cycle boundaries in the dump: re-ignition at t=41.0 and t=43.1 (2.1 s apart).
ORIGINAL slow drift: the blue core's peak index walks leftward across cycles — px 32 at t=40.0, px 22 at t=41.1, px 20 at t=43.3 — about -3.4 px/s, so the portal slides along the strip while pulsing.

PORT autocorrelation over the same late window shows no periodic structure at all (monotonic decay from lag 1, no peak above 0.4 beyond lag 6) — consistent with a frozen frame plus one flickering pixel.

Colour is wrong in both channel balance and level. Original over 20 s: meanR 61.3 vs meanB 7.4 (red-dominant by ~8x, green essentially absent at 1.8). Port: meanR 63.0 vs meanB 181.0 (blue-dominant by ~3x). The original's blue NEVER exceeds 72 on any pixel; the port holds 184 on every pixel forever.

The port does briefly produce the right colour family: at the leading edge of its expanding front there are red/orange pixels (e.g. 252,10,0 and 235,46,0 at t=4 s, 219,0,0 at t=0.5 s), so the flame palette exists in the port — it is just consumed by the violet fill within seconds and never regenerated.

Both sides are index-only / 1D in character: on a 16x16 grid the original renders as horizontal bands (a dark blue band plus red bands sweeping vertically), i.e. it drives off the flat pixel index rather than (x,y). The port's grid render agrees structurally in its first 2 s and then goes uniform.

Seed independence: seeds 7 and 1234 (30 s @ 10 fps) give identical summary stats to each other and match seed 1's character on both sides — orig mean 22 / motion 11, port mean 76 / motion 1. The divergence is not a one-seed fluke.

Window adequacy: a 240 s survey @ 2 fps shows the original still cycling with the same texture at t=240 s (no mode rotation, no regime change), and the port still solid violet at t=240 s. The pattern's full cycle (~2 s) was observed >100 times.
feedback: The port has no reset. Its lit region grows monotonically from a ~6-px seed near pixel 36 and latches every pixel it passes to a constant (63,3,184); it must decay/contract instead. The original re-ignites its core on a 2.05 s cycle: instant attack to full, ~1.0 s hold, ~1.0 s exponential fade to near-black, repeat. Whatever accumulator drives the port's radius needs to be wrapped or reset each cycle rather than integrated forever.

Target steady-state numbers on the default 60-px strip: original meanBrightness ~23 (14-35), motion avg ~9, motionLit avg ~11, zeroMotionFrames 0. The port currently sits at meanBrightness 82-83 flat with motion 0 and 393/400 zero-motion frames — it must be moving on essentially every frame.

Palette balance is inverted. The original is red-dominant: meanR ~61 vs meanB ~7 over a 20 s window, with green almost absent (meanG ~2, per-pixel G rarely above 35). Roughly two thirds of the strip should be red flame texture at any instant (25-34 of 60 pixels above R=30) and only ~19-20 pixels should be the indigo core.

Cap the blue. The original's core never exceeds blue=72 on any pixel and its red component there stays around 18 (colour approx 18,0,72 — a deep, dark indigo). The port holds 184 blue on every pixel, ~2.5x too bright and far too saturated in violet.

Restore the flame texture. The original's non-core pixels are high-frequency red ripples that change every frame (motionLit ~11, individual pixels swinging from 0 to 255 within 0.1 s). The port draws a flat fill with no per-pixel texture at all once the front passes.

Add the core's slow drift: the original's indigo core translates along the strip at roughly -3.4 px/s (peak index 32 -> 22 -> 20 over ~3.3 s) while it pulses. The port's feature is centred near pixel 36-38 and only expands, never translates.
Not an fps bug: the port's fill takes 6.4-6.9 s at 10/20/40 fps, so timing is already frame-rate independent. Do not chase frame-rate coupling; chase the missing per-cycle reset.

Scale check after fixing: on a 16x16 grid rig (256 px) the original still reads as banded 1D structure driven off the flat pixel index — the fix should keep that index-only character rather than becoming (x,y)-driven.
Sanity target for a fixed port: autocorrelation of meanBrightness at 20 fps should show a peak at lag ~41 frames (2.05 s) with harmonics at 82/123/164, matching the original.
